newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil closes softer, Brent crude off lows.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil closes softer, Brent crude off lows.

text.p: IPE June gas oil ended Tuesday softer as eyes turned to the upcoming American Petroleum Institute (API) weekly U.S. statistics and news that a large U.S. refinery is being tested prior to restarting, brokers said.
June gas oil closed down 50 cents at $173.25 a tonne while July lost just 25 cents to end the day at $174.25 a tonne.
The prompt June contract came under some pressure earlier as NYMEX crude and products came off their highs pressured by news that a major U.S. refinery may be restarting operations soon.
June Brent traded at 1648 GMT off seven cents at $19.65 a barrel.
The active July contract traded unchanged at $19.47.
The prompt June Brent contract expires on Thursday.

Preliminary estimates by traders for the weekly U.S. stock figures from the API for the week ended May 9 were for a crude build of 0.75 million barrels, a build on distillates of 2.2 million barrels and an increase in gasoline stocks of one million barrels.

A fire at a 132,500 barrel per day Citgo refinery in the U.S. saw gasoline rise on ACCESS earlier. But testing prior to the restart of Tosco Corp's Pennsylvanian refinery took much of the heat out of the market.
The plant is expected to add about 100,000 bpd to the Atlantic basin gasoline market.
